name: ZXCT1107QSA-7
title: ZXCT1107Q, ZXCT1109Q, ZXCT1110Q: automotive micropower high-side current monitors
summary: Three line-powered, unipolar high-side current monitors with a current output. The drop across a supply-side shunt gives 4 mA of output current per volt, and one resistor to ground turns that into a voltage. The sense inputs work from 2.5 V to 36 V common mode with 3 µA quiescent current. The ZXCT1107Q and ZXCT1109Q are three-pin SOT23 parts without a ground pin, mirror images of each other; the ZXCT1110Q in SOT25 adds a ground pin. All are AEC-Q100 Grade 1 qualified and PPAP capable.
key_figures: 2.5 V to 36 V (ZXCT1107Q/09Q minimum VOUT(MAX) + 2.5 V)

circuits.title: Basic application circuit, ZXCT1107Q or ZXCT1109Q
circuits.description: High-side sensing with a shunt between the supply and the load. The drop across the shunt drives an output current of 4 mA/V into RGAIN, which turns it into a ground-referred voltage for a comparator, an amplifier or an ADC. The chip takes its power from S+ and has no ground pin; its output pin is also its substrate.
notes: The ZXCT1109Q uses the same circuit with S+ and S- on swapped pins.

circuits.title: Basic application circuit, ZXCT1110Q
circuits.description: The same high-side shunt arrangement with the ZXCT1110Q, whose own GND pin goes to circuit ground. The output current, 4 mA/V of sense voltage, flows into RGAIN to give the output voltage.

circuits.title: Example circuit using ZXCT1107Q/09Q
circuits.description: Design example: a 12 V supply with a 2 A load, giving 2 V out within ±6 % using 1 % resistors. A 100 mV sense voltage keeps the chip's error at 3.4 %; RSENSE = 100 mV / 2 A = 50 mΩ and RGAIN = 2 V / (0.004 × 0.1) = 5 kΩ, rounded to 5.1 kΩ, which leaves a +2 % systematic error.

circuits.title: Example circuit using ZXCT1110Q
circuits.description: The same 12 V, 2 A, 2 V ±6 % target met with the ZXCT1110Q at a lower sense voltage. Equation 4 with ε = 4 % gives 37.2 mV, so 18.6 mΩ, rounded to 20 mΩ for 40 mV of sense voltage; RGAIN = 2 V / (0.004 × 0.04) = 12.5 kΩ, rounded to 13 kΩ.

circuits.title: Protection and EMC filtering, ZXCT1107Q or ZXCT1109Q
circuits.description: A shorted or overloaded load can put much of the supply across the sense pins while the reservoir capacitor discharges. RPROT in series with S- holds the pin current inside the ±8.5 mA rating, and with C1 across the inputs it forms a low-pass filter that cuts VHF and UHF pick-up, which would otherwise rectify inside the chip and shift its bias.
notes: C1 sits right at the S+ and S- pins.
The S+ and S- traces run only to the shunt's pads.

circuits.title: Protection and EMC filtering, ZXCT1110Q
circuits.description: A shorted or overloaded load can put much of the supply across the sense pins while the reservoir capacitor discharges. RPROT in series with S- holds the pin current inside the ±8.5 mA rating, and with C1 across the inputs it forms a low-pass filter that cuts VHF and UHF pick-up, which would otherwise rectify inside the chip and shift its bias.
notes: C1 sits right at the S+ and S- pins.

circuits.title: 400 V current monitor
circuits.description: Current sensing on a 200 V to 450 V rail, as in an electric vehicle. The 500 V PNP Q1 between OUT and RGAIN takes up most of the rail voltage, and the 12 V zener D1, biased through R1 from the rail, sets the voltage the monitor sees. D2 clamps the sense inputs under overload and so caps the output current near 3 mA; with RGAIN a few kΩ the output stays at a few volts, and a higher gain may need its own output clamp diode.

parts.note: sets the zener bias for the supply range

notes: U1 may be a ZXCT1107Q, ZXCT1109Q or ZXCT1110Q; with the ZXCT1110Q its GND pin joins the BIAS node at Q1's base.

circuits.title: Test circuit for pulse response
circuits.description: The monitor is run from a negative supply with S+ at 0 V. A 50 Ω pulse generator, terminated in 50 Ω, drives S- through 1 kΩ, and S- returns to S+ through another 1 kΩ; the output develops across 10 kΩ to the negative rail and is watched with an oscilloscope.

circuits.title: Test circuit for CMRR
circuits.description: A 10 mV AC source is coupled through 2200 µF onto the S+ node, which is fed from +20 V through 50 Ω. A 1 kΩ sense resistor bypassed by 470 µF and 100 nF joins S+ to S-, and 9.1 kΩ plus 200 kΩ load S- to 0 V. Channel 1 sees the common-mode signal at S+; channel 2 sees the output across 2.5 kΩ.

circuits.title: Test circuit for small signal bandwidth
circuits.description: S+ sits on a +20 V supply bypassed by 2200 µF and 1 µF. A 10 mVpp AC source with a 50 Ω termination is coupled through 2200 µF onto S-, which joins S+ through 1 kΩ and is loaded to 0 V by 200 kΩ. Channel 1 sees the input at S-; channel 2 sees the output across 2.5 kΩ.

operation.text: A high-side, unipolar current monitor: it senses across a shunt in the supply line, so the ground plane stays whole. It needs no supply pin of its own, drawing its power from S+, with a quiescent current of 3 µA. Its output is a current; one external resistor sets the gain.

All three share one application topology. The ZXCT1110Q adds a GND pin, which lowers the output offset current and so the absolute error. The ZXCT1107Q and ZXCT1109Q have no ground pin; their pinouts are mirror images of each other, for small layouts.

ZXCT11 XX Q XX -7: the device variant 07 has its sense pins placed as on the ZXCT1110, 09 as on the ZXCT1009, 10 as on the ZXCT1010; Q is automotive compliant; SA is SOT23 and W5 is SOT25; -7 is 7-inch tape and reel.

On the ZXCT1107Q and ZXCT1109Q the OUT pin doubles as the substrate, so the rail at S+ must be at least 2.5 V above VOUT. For the ZXCT1110Q the output may reach VS- - 1 V; to avoid added error the supply should exceed VOUT by 1.5 V, a margin that can drop to 1.0 V at VSENSE = 100 mV.

Under 10 mV of sense voltage, internal offsets can take the output current down to its zero-signal level (for the ZXCT1107Q/09Q, the IOUT at VSENSE = 0), so the reading may not differ from that at no load. Measurement with VSENSE under 10 mV is not recommended.

The shunt is a trade between efficiency and accuracy: small enough that its drop does not starve the load, large enough that the device's errors, mostly random, stay small at the threshold current where the system must act. The total error is the device error plus the tolerances of RSENSE and RGAIN; device error shrinks as VSENSE grows.

The sense inputs are rated to +0.8 V differential, but survive more if the current into S+ or S- is held within ±8.5 mA. A 4.7 kΩ resistor in series with S- does this without adding much measurement error.

RF picked up on the supply or load wiring can rectify inside the chip and shift its bias. RPROT with a 10 pF to 47 pF leadless ceramic capacitor across S+ and S- forms a low-pass filter that attenuates VHF and UHF.

Copper and solder drops on the way to RSENSE cause visible error from about 1 A up. Give the shunt the widest copper possible, run the S+ and S- traces only to the shunt's own pads, and put the filter capacitor C1, if fitted, very close to the S+ and S- pins.
The SOT23 outline carries a 7° angle on all marked faces; the SOT25 lead angle α runs from 0° to 8°.
Each package carries its four-character identification code (1107, 1109 or 1110) on the top face.
